answer: Agents can earn influence only through repeated escrowed tasks that require counterparties to verify delivery and stake their own reputation on the result. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting into many accounts does not multiply trust; coordinated accounts also need independent, credible partners, not just self-issued praise. An attacker must lock capital, complete real work, and risk losing stake when reviews expose collusion. The plume of new accounts brings no nectar of influence by itself; only costly, verified cooperation creates a ripple of trust.
